notes.summary: 2026-10 epoch retune. Joint objective w|d|_ET + 0.01 s/(km/h) x w|d|_trap, grouped 5-fold CV by benchmark row, one-standard-error rule toward the simplest (most neutral) knob set; clusters with < 8 bound bikes or < 6 distinct benchmark rows not fitted. Result (epoch rules): ET w|d| 0.2627 s / bias +0.0153 s (n 266); legacy rules 0.2646 / +0.0135 (n 276) vs the published 0.2629 / +0.0073. Trap weighted bias +13.8 -> +1.1 km/h (w|d| 14.6 -> 5.8). Top speed (83 matched) mean|d| 28.1 -> 13.3 km/h, bias +24.3 -> +5.4, within +/-20 km/h 41 -> 65. All sims on the Rust core (NativeEngine, bit-identical to the Python reference; spot-checked on the 3 references + 14 catalog bikes across 6 clusters with the new knobs).

acceptance.et_criterion: epoch rules 0.2627 <= 0.2629; legacy rules +0.0017 (inside the +0.005 window) with large trap/top-speed gains
acceptance.trap_criterion: weighted trap bias +1.12 km/h (epoch rules) / +1.09 (legacy) vs +13.83
acceptance.conservative_note: The full epoch does not regress ET w|d| by more than 0.005 s vs 0.2629 under either rule set, so no epoch item needs dropping. The subset hybrids (data-only, physics-only) are in old_vs_new for context; untuned they are worse than both HEAD and the retuned full epoch. 'conservative_alternatives' instead records knob-set alternatives for the orchestrator (see knob_alternatives).

The references' top end is too strong (K5 trap 240.8 at the pre-retune grip 1.08 vs 233 published) — physics/data-limited, not knob-reachable.

Weighted-L1 fit (weights 1.0/0.7/0.5): mu 0.888 -> K5 10.188 (outside +/-0.10). The minimax fit is the only one that keeps all three inside their documented bands.

notes.lambda_justification: lam = 0.01 s per km/h (a 1 km/h trap error costs as much as 0.01 s of ET). Outlet-to-outlet agreement for the same bike is ~0.1-0.2 s on ET and ~5-10 km/h on trap (66-ft trap average vs instantaneous finish speed, GPS vs beams, mph/km/h transcription) -> noise ratio ~0.02 s per km/h; the HEAD corpus residual scales (ET ~0.26 s vs trap ~15 km/h) give ~0.017. Weighting trap at about half its noise equivalent lets it break ties without overriding the ET headline. Sensitivity: lam 0 and 0.01 select identical knobs for every cluster; lam 0.03 changes ONE cluster (litre_sport_195p -> launch_rpm_factor 0.60 at rated grip, because mu < 1 also lowers trap by ~6 km/h on that cluster) at an ET cost of +0.010 s on the headline (alternative 'conservative_lam003').

It mainly moves bikes whose rated peak-torque rpm sits at 0.62-0.70 x redline (Streetfighter V4, Hayabusa Gen2/Gen3, Z H2, M1000RR, RSV4).
